assumptions: No new factual assumption or unanswered requirement is introduced. Packaging, API and next edition choices remain proposed decisions requiring exact canonical revision approval.

Future implementation rechecks edition availability, source/target hashes, actual owner and action-specific scope. Any changed baseline is revised before execution rather than treated as an approved assumption.

differences.complementary: Functional ontology and explicit root/preservation controls from A are combined with B's exact ontology integration owner, linked receipt and first-authored-preparation mechanics. TASK-002 through TASK-016 define the resulting shared boundaries.
differences.evidence: Both candidate source inventories match current files. Direct inspection confirms core-only imports, empty starter graphs, configured-file-only preview/publication, config scope exclusion, authored-ontology protection and active initializer v9 versus source/Template v11. Guard report wording is 20 passes and one setup fixture failure, followed by corrected installed results; no integration evidence is inferred.
differences.exclusive: The competing config-write boundaries and renderer location are resolved by the explicit narrow ontology integration owner and pure shared renderer. Refresh requires an explicit selector. These are design alternatives permitted by the TRD, not conflicting mandatory requirements; no mutually exclusive commitment remains.
differences.scope: Root helper/resource adoption remains separate from source/Template distribution. Root additive ontology config and canonical semantics use one selected ontology-owner integration transaction; child initialization coordinates that owner for existing authored installations and retains setup authority for absent/pristine starters.
differences.terminology: Use one neutral recipe path and curator-ontology-1.0.0 integration edition. Integration record schema 2 is distinct from unchanged runtime/config module_version 1.0.0 and proposed governance-starter-v12; exact values remain proposed pending plan approval.

interfaces: Recipe -> pure ontology-owned renderer -> destination-local module project graph, binding graph and competency files; stable namespace, installed source hashes and unchanged core/context are validated before writes.

Existing authored ontology -> distinct integrate-curator proposal/grant -> candidate-config/graph preview -> current-owner guarded immutable transaction/recovery in existing control_records/ontology. Ordinary publish/grant/config contracts stay unchanged.

Initializer -> finalized destination identity/governance -> initial setup write scope or current ontology owner -> linked immutable operation receipt -> static integrated verification -> existing setup/module history. Canonical completion precedes setup success.

Reusable source -> checked registered Template -> neutral complete capability. Active root helper/resource adoption and exact ontology integration adoption remain separately selected; generic root project initialization and bulk product adoption are excluded.

Ontology discovery -> current canonical owner inspection -> permitted manual/session action; declaration, configuration, installation, compatibility, authorization, pending delivery, completed outcome and observed runtime remain distinct.
omitted: Solver A proposed separate root ontology.yaml configuration adoption followed by ordinary publish is replaced with Solver B's narrow single ontology integration transaction. Existing code cannot preview proposed config and its core grant cannot select ontology.yaml, so the final plan explicitly implements candidate-config validation and a distinct exact adoption grant while preserving ordinary publish semantics.

Solver A renderer ownership under initializer is moved to the ontology owner as a pure shared function so both child setup and root integration consume one validated byte producer; initializer retains setup state and action ownership.

Duplicate recipe directories, edition spellings and verification report roots are consolidated into ONTOLOGY-depo/integrations/curator/1.0.0, curator-ontology-1.0.0 and Verification/integrated-curator-ontology. No semantic requirement is removed.

Solver B's potentially ambiguous changed-source adoption refresh is replaced by explicit --refresh-module curator. This preserves Solver A's clear refresh gate and the approved ordinary-rerun contract; initial --adopt-module curator still supplies both integrations.

Separate duplicated route verification tasks and neutral checks are incorporated into TASK-012 and TASK-013 with explicit cases and criteria. The final 23-task structure retains every bounded result rather than concatenating both task lists.
requirements: All 14 original requirement IDs, exact outcomes, 34 verbatim acceptance clauses and original dependency arrays are retained active with empty evidence. No requirement is dispositioned away.

Forward coverage covers every inspected source and every active requirement; reverse coverage maps all 23 tasks and 7 phases to the supplied scope. TASK-012/013 cover Template plus new/first/manual/prior routes; TASK-017/018/019/020/021 cover session, pending owner, staged Task, browser and health obligations.
retained: Solver A retained: full action/function and current-owner distinctions, source/Template/root ownership separation, exact root adoption without project.json or v9 initializer replacement, neutral recipe completeness, detailed route/preservation/recovery controls and final source-settle ordering.

Solver B retained: separate ontology-owned integration config-selection/publication/recovery, typed local recipe and current-source semantics, first authored preparation path, versioned linked receipt lineage, full setup matrix and explicit actual owner/browser evidence.
Both candidates retained: all 14 exact TRD outcomes and 34 verbatim acceptance clauses with original dependencies and source-grounded negatives; no integration execution or premature readiness claim.
risks: New integration config authority and candidate-config preview are necessary bounded interfaces and must preserve legacy publication/grants, disabled choices, enabled guards, exact source/target ownership and immutable recovery.

Cross-owner setup and ontology commits are not claimed atomic. Explicit lock order, original intent/pre/post states, linked completion receipt, partial diagnostics and identical-request recovery prevent false setup completion.

Custom/incomplete packages, missing owner or publication authority, legacy role layouts, collisions and changed source/target versions remain preserved named holds. No matching bytes or registry membership confers overwrite authority.
Future native owner, service/browser, real product and external observations are unexercised. Their missing scope cannot be replaced with fixtures, configured flags or historical reports.
verification: Senior inspected both complete candidates and directly checked the approved TRD, complete role pair, baseline, installed planning contract, relevant live ontology/setup/guard interfaces and source hashes.

Read-only structural/lifecycle/source/coverage validation is recorded in validation.json; exact source/role/candidate hashes and source path safety are recorded in source-validation.json. No managed-plan or runtime mutation is used for these checks.
